nodes.question: What kind of approaches are suggested for the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity?
nodes.answer: Rights-based and community-led approaches are suggested for the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity.
nodes.paragraph: It is therefore all the more important that the world adopts a Figure 23: Nature Positive shared global goal for nature, to guide and drive action across by 2030 governments, business and society. A measurable global goal for nature. Source: Locke et al. (2021) 193 A global goal of reversing biodiversity loss to secure a nature- positive world by 2030 is necessary if we are to turn the tide on nature loss and safeguard the natural world for current and future generations 193 It must be our guiding star, in the same way that the goal of limiting global warming to °C, and preferably 1.5°C, guides our efforts on climate. FULL RECOVERY Action to secure a nature-positive world this decade, measured BY 2050 through an increase in the health, abundance, diversity and resilience of species, populations and ecosystems, can be taken by everyone, and also adopted nationally and ultimately globally, to ZERO NET urgently transform our relationship with nature. LOSS OF NATURE Encouragingly, momentum is building. More than 90 world leaders FROM 2020 have endorsed a Leaders' Pledge for Nature, committing to reverse biodiversity loss by 2030, and G7 have signalled their ambition to secure a nature-positive world.
